prompt: In UTF-8 the letter `ï` takes two bytes. What happens when this program runs?
choices: It panics: byte index 3 is not a character boundary
explain: String slices use byte offsets, and `n`, `a` take one byte each while `ï` takes bytes 2 and 3. Byte 3 is the middle of `ï`, so Rust panics instead of producing broken text. Use `chars().take(3)` to work with characters.
